clue.text: A sign the informer is a plant

parts.note: the zodiac sign Scorpio is pictured as the Scorpion
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: An astrologer warns that the person tipping off the police is a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sign' looks like Scorpio, but the sign's creature, the Scorpion, gives the extra N; GRASS is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpion grass is an old country name for the forget-me-not, a flowering herb.

clue.text: Aerosol supplied by son on request

parts.note: a prayer is an earnest request

explanation.surface: A spray can was provided because a boy asked for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that sprays its contents, a sprayer.

clue.text: Away from the pin, but ready for putting on

definitions.meaning: literally removed from the peg it hung on
clothes bought ready-made, ready to wear at once

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball is far from the flag but ready to be putted.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg clothing is ready-made rather than tailored, so it can be worn at once.

clue.text: Picture stolen in post office

indicators.note: the stolen word goes inside the post office letters

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A painting was taken in a robbery at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Better away football kit

parts.note: out means away, not at home
a strip is a team's football kit

explanation.surface: A team's change shirts are an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: STRIP is the British word for a team's matching football kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to surpass or do better than someone.

clue.text: Good introduction to people of a particular sort

parts.note: an entry is an introduction or way in

explanation.surface: A fine way of meeting a certain class of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentry denotes a class of people, especially the landed upper class, often used ironically.

clue.text: Going berserk, lad stared with legs wide apart

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, signalling these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A boy ran amok and stood with feet planted wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Astraddle means straddling, sitting or standing with a leg on each side.

clue.text: Endlessly flourish old 'soldier's headgear

indicators.note: the last letter of the flourish word is cut off

parts.note: to flourish a stick is to shake or brandish it

explanation.surface: An old soldier keeps waving his hat about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the E off SHAKE, leaving SHAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military cap with a plume.

clue.text: Baffled by cookery adviser's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the name is heard rather than read

parts.note: Mrs Beeton wrote the famous Victorian Book of Household Management

explanation.surface: A listener is puzzled by a radio chef.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton was Britain's classic Victorian cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten can mean defeated or stumped, unable to solve something.

clue.text: Offer for sale again, having regard to the petty cash

parts.note: re is the formal word for 'with regard to', 'concerning'
a float is the small sum of cash kept in a till to give change

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts goods back on sale, keeping an eye on the till money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is only a link. To float a company is to offer its shares for sale, so refloating is doing it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To float a business is to launch its shares on the market; refloating repeats that offer.

clue.text: Eccentric head starts action

parts.note: nut is informal for the head
an action at law is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A peculiar leader sets a campaign going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' is a link word, not an instruction to take first letters; ACTION is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a slang term for a crazy or very odd person, an eccentric.

clue.text: Half-hearted hooray upset a crude fellow

indicators.note: upset signals that the remaining letters are knocked over into a new order
the heart of the six-letter word is its middle pair, and losing one of those two letters leaves it half-hearted

explanation.surface: A muted cheer knocks over a boorish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the R, one of the two middle letters, gives HOOAY, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo, from Swift's Gulliver's Travels, is a coarse, brutish lout.

clue.text: Go off a boxing match, having change of heart

parts.note: milk that goes off is said to turn sour
a bout is a single contest in boxing

explanation.surface: A spectator leaves a prize fight, having had second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, the same as a change of mind.

clue.text: State of old fossil, perhaps, seen around the bar

indicators.note: the relic is seen around, enclosing, the bar word

parts.note: a fossil is an example of a relic, something surviving from the past
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: The condition of an old codger who is always to be found near the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old fossil' suggests an elderly regular, but it is a relic; 'State' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state governed without a monarch.

clue.text: Mate getting near the knuckle, say, in Coalport

indicators.note: the knuckle word comes near, just before, the mate word

parts.note: a knuckle is an example of a bone
china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A friend's jokes are getting rather risqué in a Shropshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near the knuckle' means risqué, but here the knuckle is just a bone. Coalport is a famous English porcelain maker; china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalport is an English maker of fine porcelain, an example of the ware.

clue.text: Exceptional relative thought likely to succeed

parts.note: odd here means out of the ordinary
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: An unusual family member is tipped for success.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse at odds-on is the betting favourite, expected to win.

clue.text: Way I cut flower?

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way
I is the Roman numeral for one
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether to trim a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a sedum, a succulent plant bearing small flowers.

clue.text: I sent off this man in the games in Greece

indicators.note: sent off means dispatched in disarray, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee explains he dismissed this player in the Greek tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: the Isthmian Games were held at Corinth in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmian describes the ancient Games held on the Isthmus of Corinth.

clue.text: Implore unit to shove off

parts.note: to implore is to beg
one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A sergeant pleads with his platoon to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an imperative telling someone to go away, like 'shove off'.

clue.text: Person on the rink in tight-fitting costume?

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person
a rink is a sheet of ice

explanation.surface: A skater on the rink wears a snug outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress.

clue.text: Celestial body caused interference on radio set

indicators.note: interference scrambles the signal, signalling these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A passing heavenly body made the wireless crackle.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, a celestial body.

clue.text: Idealist briefly had American juice extractor

parts.note: had is shortened to 'd as in I'd
a reamer is the American name for a lemon squeezer

explanation.surface: A dreamy person owned a US gadget for squeezing fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone who pursues ideals rather than practical things.

clue.text: Pretty girl given work, serving food, perhaps

parts.note: a doll is slang for an attractive girl
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A pretty waitress is given a job dishing up food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; 'food, perhaps' tells you the serving is of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of food served out.

clue.text: Attractive girl with cold reluctant to use this drying agent

parts.note: a dish is informal for a good-looking person
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling

explanation.surface: A pretty girl with a chill doesn't want to touch the washing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use this' links wordplay to the definition; the cloth is the agent that dries the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is a cloth used to wipe and dry crockery.

clue.text: Second man's wages

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it, so 'man's' is crews read as crew plus s

explanation.surface: An assistant's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang for a person's wages or salary.

clue.text: Foreigner married in the London area

indicators.note: the married word is placed inside the postal area

parts.note: SE is a London postal district, south-east
wed means married

explanation.surface: An overseas visitor got married in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is a London postcode area (south-east London).
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, so a foreigner to the British setter.

clue.text: Organisation put in dangerous position

definitions.meaning: to frame someone or put them in harm's way

explanation.definitionFit: A setup is an arrangement, and to be set up is to be framed.

clue.text: Stopper finally removed, face a drink

indicators.note: the last letter of the stopper word is taken away

parts.note: a cork is a bottle stopper
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: With the cork pulled out, someone faces up to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally removed' drops the K from CORK, leaving COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit drink or liqueur.

clue.text: Caretaker intervening

definitions.meaning: a caretaker government or manager holds office temporarily
the intervening period is the meantime between two events

explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes something provisional, and also the time in between events.

clue.text: It makes an attractive present — conclusion of writer in The Times, for example

indicators.note: the final letter is put inside the newspaper description

parts.note: The Times was printed in Wapping, East London, so it is a Wapping paper

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A journalist's closing piece in the newspaper is a lovely gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is the East London district where The Times was produced from 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping paper is what makes a gift look attractive when it is given.
